title: Pacific-islands expected shortfall for the forecast period

claims.text: The expected shortfall is a positive-part tail measure: it is the conditional average revenue shortfall across the joint simulation draws in which the Pacific-islands aggregate loss exceeds its value-at-risk threshold. Risk is defined as neutral revenue minus event revenue; gains are retained in the signed distribution, so the mean loss and the tail shortfall are distinct quantities, and this measure applies only to the positive shortfall.
The Pacific-islands figure is a joint aggregate computed from common simulation draws across the modeled Pacific island countries; country quantiles are never summed.

limitations: Historical input provenance for this assessment is incomplete; the bundle is provided for inspection only and is not recomputable.
The measure is conditional on the event scenario and climate forecast vintage recorded in the assessment metadata; it is not an unconditional or causal attribution.

The expected shortfall is a positive-part shortfall on the aggregate revenue-loss distribution and must not be read as the signed mean loss, which can be smaller because gains are retained in the signed distribution.
The figure covers agriculture, forestry and fishing value added with conditional government revenue transmission; it is not a total-economy loss and not a sovereign default probability.
Monetary outcomes are expressed in constant 2025 USD at a fixed 2025 exchange rate; price and exchange-rate responses are not modeled.
The assessment does not claim predictive skill for any individual year; convergence diagnostics alone do not establish predictive skill.
